sections.h2: Who taxes and bills a Cincinnati house
sections.html:
The city of Cincinnati does not send a property tax bill. Hamilton County does. Two county offices handle it. The auditor decides what each parcel is worth, and the treasurer mails the bills and collects. You will find the treasurer's staff in Room 402, 138 East Court Street, or reach them at 513-946-4800 on weekdays from 8 to 4.

A three-person Board of Revision hears value disputes. Its seats belong to the auditor, the treasurer and the commissioners' president. The city levies tax and gets its share of the proceeds, but it never values or bills your house.

Expect two bills a year. For 2026 the first half went out in mid-January with a February deadline, while the second half was mailed in early July and due in late July. The second pair of dates was moved late because state legislation requiring an Inflation Cap Credit forced the treasurer to recalculate second-half bills. Dates can shift in other years, so read the deadline printed on your bill.

  • A payment that comes in during the ten days after the deadline carries a 5 percent penalty. Later than that, the penalty is 10 percent.
  • To ask for a penalty to be reviewed, download the Penalty Remit Application from the treasurer's site.
  • No discount is given for paying early, but a prepayment plan named TOP lets owners pay ahead in installments.

There are four ways to pay.

  • Online through Point & Pay. The vendor, not the county, charges $1.00 for an eCheck or 2.35 percent on a credit card.
  • By phone to the same vendor at 1-877-764-3524.
  • By mail, with a personal check, cashier's check or money order made out to Hamilton County Treasurer. Write the stub or parcel number on the memo line.
  • At the Room 402 counter, the only place that takes cash.

Mail counts as on time when postmarked by the due date. Trouble is, the Postal Service postmark reflects when a machine sorts the envelope, possibly after the day you dropped it off. When the deadline is close, give the envelope to a clerk and request a hand stamp.

The county taxes 35 percent of market value, called assessed value, and states every rate in mills, where a mill means $1 for each $1,000 of assessed value. Voted levies are tempered by a reduction factor so they stay close to what voters approved, even as values climb. Then the state subtracts credits: non-business for residential property, owner occupancy, and homestead.

Your bill shows the county levies below plus separate lines for school district, township and city or village. Great Oaks career campus levies apply in every Hamilton County school district except Cincinnati and Northwest.

Owners who believe the market value is too high can file a complaint with the Board of Revision from January 1 through March 31. Call the board at 513-946-4035 and find forms on its website. The cutoff under section 5715.19 is March 31 following the tax year, or the close of first-half collection when that comes later. A postmark on or before that day saves a mailed filing.

A complaint can attack market value and nothing else, because local levies are not open to challenge. Until the board rules, you are allowed to pay on the lower value your complaint claims.

Once a payment is missed, penalties and interest begin to build. A phone call to 513-946-4800 can set up a delinquent contract that breaks past-due amounts into scheduled payments, as long as new bills are paid on time. While the contract stays in good standing, the house is shielded from added penalties, interest, foreclosure and a lien sale.

  • Balances left after second-half collection are certified delinquent that November. They can enter a lien sale the following October, usually near mid-month.
  • Eligible liens are sold to financial institutions in one negotiated block, not one by one to individuals, and extra fees attach once a lien is sold.
  • A tax foreclosure is a lawsuit filed by the county prosecutor. Owners typically get 28 days to answer the summons, and a judgment leads to an online sheriff's sale.

Ohio's homestead exemption reaches Cincinnati owners through the county auditor. The 2026 credit covers the tax on $29,700 of value for qualifying seniors and disabled owners whose income is within $41,000. Disabled owners who are former service members get the tax on $59,400 of value, with no income test.

One credit takes no paperwork: the stadium sales tax credit goes automatically to owners who already receive the 2.5 percent rollback on an owner-occupied home. Homestead forms, however, are due December 31 of the year you want the credit.

The city is made of 52 neighborhoods on hills and ridges. Three places, Norwood, Elmwood Place and St. Bernard, are enclaves with their own governments, so check which jurisdiction a street belongs to. The July 2025 population estimate is 314,367, owners hold 39.8 percent of homes, and the typical owner's home is worth $230,900. With under four in ten homes owner-occupied, many sellers are landlords or heirs, and each parcel's tax status should be checked separately.

Unpaid tax stays with the parcel, and a title search will find it. Request a payoff figure from the treasurer that includes earlier years and hand it to the closing agent. If the lien has already been sold, the treasurer can name the buyer of the lien, and your payoff will include that holder's added fees.

An owner who is behind but wants to keep the house can sign a delinquent contract before the lien sale, which keeps the parcel out of it as long as current taxes are paid. A cash buyer can close quickly, provided the title company pays the tax balance out of your proceeds at the table. Bring your latest bill and parcel number to the closing, and ask the title agent to confirm in writing that nothing remains owed.

faqs.q: What number reaches the office that sends Cincinnati tax bills?
faqs.a: Dial 513-946-4800 for the Hamilton County Treasurer, open weekdays. Value questions go to the Board of Revision at 513-946-4035.

faqs.q: When is the second-half Cincinnati bill due?
faqs.a: In the 2026 cycle it was due in late July, after a late change caused by the Inflation Cap Credit. Dates can differ in other years, so check the printed bill.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to a late Cincinnati property tax payment?
faqs.a: Five percent during the first ten days after the due date, then 10 percent. A Penalty Remit Application is available on the treasurer's site.

faqs.q: What is the filing window for a Cincinnati value complaint?
faqs.a: January 1 through March 31. The complaint goes to the Hamilton County Board of Revision, and mail postmarked by March 31 counts.

faqs.q: Can unpaid taxes cost me my Cincinnati house?
faqs.a: Only through foreclosure. A lien sale moves the lien, not the house, and the holder may start foreclosure after a year. A delinquent contract signed before the sale, with current taxes paid, keeps the parcel off the list.
